title: Japan Pledges $15.5 Million in Anti-Terror Funds

image.attribution: U.S. Department of State from United States / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Japan has pledged $15.5 million to help countries in the Middle East and Africa that are battling militants from the Islamic State group.

Tokyo’s Foreign Minister Fumio Kishida said Tuesday the aid would support counter-terrorism efforts, including increased border control and investigation capabilities.

More details of the aid will be unveiled by Vice Foreign Minister Yasuhide at an international anti-terror conference Thursday in Washington, a foreign ministry statement said.

The counter-terrorism package is twice the amount previously pledged by Kishida during a visit to Brussels last month. Separately, Tokyo has also pledged $200 million to help refugees fleeing Islamic State-controlled areas.

Prime Minister Shinzo Abe has vowed a tough response to the Islamic State militants, who in January beheaded two Japanese hostages – a journalist and his companion.

questions.question: What will the money pledged by Japan be used for?
options: A. To strengthen military forces in Japan
B. To support counter-terrorism efforts in the Middle East and Africa
C. To increase trade relations with Europe
D. To aid in the reconstruction of war-torn countries in Asia
questions.answer: B. To support counter-terrorism efforts in the Middle East and Africa

questions.question: What did the Japanese Foreign Minister say about the financial aid?
options: A. It will be used exclusively for military training
B. It focuses on enhancing border control and investigation capabilities
C. It is intended as a gift to improve diplomatic relations
D. The funding is conditional upon receiving assistance from the UN
questions.answer: B. It focuses on enhancing border control and investigation capabilities

questions.question: What else is Japan doing to help refugees?
options: A. Providing financial aid to neighboring Asian countries
B. Offering resettlement programs for refugees in Japan
C. Pledging $200 million to assist refugees fleeing Islamic State-controlled areas
D. Creating job opportunities for refugees in Japan
questions.answer: C. Pledging $200 million to assist refugees fleeing Islamic State-controlled areas
